imd._note: IMD's latest extended-range outlook, refreshed by the Nykas Daily Refresh when IMD issues a new one (usually Thursdays). categories: above / near / below for an IMD sub-division only when IMD states it; otherwise left out.
imd.title: IMD extended range forecast (weekly press release), 26 November 2026: current weather status and extended range forecast for the next two weeks (26 November to 9 December 2026)
imd.summary: For 26 November to 2 December IMD expects normal rainfall over South Peninsular India, with isolated heavy rain over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal and Kerala on 26–27 November. For 3–9 December rainfall is likely to be normal to above normal over South Peninsular India, increasing in the first half of the week; Rayalaseema and Andhra Pradesh are not given a separate rainfall outlook.

weeks.label: Week 1
weeks.text: Normal rainfall activity is likely over South Peninsular India and below normal over the rest of the country; fairly widespread to widespread rain likely over Kerala & Mahe and Lakshadweep on 26–28 November.

regional_text.Rayalaseema: Not named for rainfall; IMD only mentions strong surface winds over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and Rayalaseema on 26–28 November. The nearest statement is normal rainfall over South Peninsular India as a whole.
regional_text.Tamil Nadu: Isolated heavy rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal (and Kerala & Mahe) on 26–27 November.

weeks.label: Week 2
weeks.text: Rainfall is likely to be normal to above normal over South Peninsular India, increasing in the first half of the week.

regional_text.Rayalaseema: Not named individually; IMD expects normal to above-normal rainfall over South Peninsular India as a whole.
regional_text.Tamil Nadu: Isolated heavy rainfall likely over Tamil Nadu and Kerala on some days of the week.

season.text: IMD's monthly outlook for November 2026: rainfall over South Peninsular India (Tamil Nadu, Puducherry & Karaikal, Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam, Rayalaseema, Kerala & Mahe and South Interior Karnataka taken together) is most likely to be below normal (less than 77% of the long-period average of about 118.7 mm).
